title: Cardiac catheterization
description: Cardiac catheterization is a diagnostic procedure where your doctor threads a thin, flexible tube called a catheter through your blood vessels to examine your heart and coronary arteries. This test helps diagnose heart disease, assess how well your heart is pumping, measure blood pressure in your heart chambers, and take tissue samples if needed. Your doctor can see blockages, valve problems, and other abnormalities on X-ray imaging. The procedure is performed while you're awake but sedated, and you'll generally feel minimal discomfort. This detailed information helps your doctor plan the best treatment for your condition, whether that's medication, a stent, bypass surgery, or another intervention.
